market_outlook: This is a company-specific earnings note with no broad directional market commentary provided. No explicit bull or bear lean is expressed at the index level.

company_items.summary: AutoZone beat FQ4 EPS estimates ($56.05 vs. $54.03 consensus), but the quality was low — the upside was driven by tariff refunds (145bp gross margin tailwind) and a non-cash LIFO benefit (105bp tailwind) rather than core execution. Domestic comps missed badly at +1.6% vs. the Street's +3.1%, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100bp year-over-year. Management noted improving sales linearity in the final 8 weeks and expressed confidence heading into fiscal 2027.

Cognex announced the acquisition of RealSense, the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI, for approximately $500MM upfront plus an additional ~$106.5MM. RealSense is expected to generate $80-90MM in revenue, representing more than 50% year-over-year growth, making this a meaningful bet on the robotics and Physical AI buildout.

MillerKnoll delivered solid FQ1 EPS upside (53c vs. 36c consensus), and importantly the beat holds up even excluding an 11-cent tariff refund tailwind — adjusted EPS was 42c, still ahead of the Street. Sales missed, declining 3.3% organically to $923.4MM vs. $943.2MM expected, though orders rose 3.5% year-over-year. Full-year sales guidance was trimmed modestly while EPS guidance was left unchanged, and FQ2 EPS guidance is roughly in line with consensus.

Pentair named Bob Hau as its new CFO effective November 1st, with current interim CFO Bob Fishman staying on through that date to ensure a smooth transition. Hau brings significant blue-chip CFO experience, having previously held the role at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox International.

THOR Industries missed FQ4 EPS estimates (78c vs. 87c consensus) as gross margins fell 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4%, well below the Street's 13.85% estimate, despite revenue coming in slightly above expectations at $2.311B. Management struck a cautious tone, citing stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflation pressuring household budgets, and declined to provide formal fiscal 2027 guidance. Bright spots included healthy dealer inventory levels, structural cost actions underway, and a dramatic ~75% surge in North American towable RV order backlog year-over-year.

Viking Therapeutics shares spiked in pre-market trading after reporting positive clinical trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, with patients achieving 22% weight loss. This is a highly significant data readout that positions VK2735 as a competitive asset in the crowded but high-stakes obesity drug market.

sectors: RV/recreational vehicle sector faces headwinds per THOR Industries commentary — stubborn interest rates, fuel costs, and inflation are suppressing retail demand and compressing margins industry-wide. Robotics and Physical AI getting a positive signal via Cognex's RealSense acquisition. GLP-1/obesity drug space remains a high-momentum catalyst space following Viking's positive trial data.
tts_summary:
Good morning. This is a company-specific earnings note for Tuesday September 22nd — there is no broad macro or index-level commentary in this dispatch, so let's go straight through the names.

Starting with AutoZone. They beat on fiscal fourth quarter earnings per share — fifty-six dollars and five cents versus the Street at fifty-four dollars and three cents — but do not get too excited about that headline. The beat was low quality. Tariff refunds added 145 basis points to gross margins and a non-cash LIFO adjustment added another 105 basis points. Strip those out and the picture gets murkier fast. Domestic comps came in at plus 1.6% versus the Street expecting plus 3.1% — a meaningful miss — and operating expenses worsened 100 basis points year-over-year. Management did note improving sales linearity as the quarter progressed and said they feel well positioned for fiscal 2027 growth. Mixed read overall.

Cognex is making a significant move into Physical AI. They are acquiring RealSense — the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and robotic perception technology — for roughly 500 million dollars upfront plus about 106 million more. RealSense is tracking 80 to 90 million dollars in revenue with more than 50% year-over-year growth. This is a direct play on the robotics buildout and bullish for Cognex.

MillerKnoll had a strong quarter. They reported 53 cents versus the Street at 36 cents — and importantly, even backing out the 11-cent tariff refund tailwind, they still beat at 42 cents. Sales were light, down 3.3% organically, but orders rose 3.5% year-over-year. Full-year EPS guidance was held unchanged. This is a high-quality beat.

Pentair named Bob Hau as the new CFO effective November 1st. Hau has held the CFO seat at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox International. Largely a neutral housekeeping item.

THOR Industries missed. Fiscal fourth quarter earnings came in at 78 cents versus 87 cents expected. Gross margins fell 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4%, well below the Street's 13.85% estimate. Management was candid about the tough environment — stubborn interest rates, high fuel costs, and inflation are keeping retail soft. They declined to give formal fiscal 2027 guidance. On the positive side, dealer inventories are healthy and the North American towable RV order backlog surged roughly 75% year-over-year. Cautious read but not without some silver linings.

Finally, Viking Therapeutics is the big pre-market mover. The company reported positive trial results for its GLP-1 obesity drug, with patients achieving 22% weight loss. Shares are spiking. This keeps the obesity drug space front and center as one of the most active catalyst areas in biotech.

Bottom line for today: no index-level directional call in this note. Watch Viking for momentum in the GLP-1 trade, treat AutoZone's beat with skepticism given the quality issues, and note that the RV sector macro remains challenged per THOR's commentary.
